The rows a reader has kept, side by side

Source: R/calculator.R
mm_calculator_comparison.Rd

Taken from DynNom, which is the one thing that package does that this one did not: a prediction on its own answers nothing, and the question a reader actually has is what the number would be if one value were different. So rows accumulate and are drawn against a common scale, so two of them can be compared. Each row shows its estimate as a dot; no uncertainty range is drawn beside it, by owner decision on review finding D-1. The bounds are still carried in each record for anyone working with the numbers rather than reading the screen.

Usage

mm_calculator_comparison(
  saved,
  threshold,
  higher_is = "worse",
  subject = "patient",
  specs = NULL
)

Arguments

saved

A list of kept rows, each with values, pred and extrapolated. lower and upper are accepted and retained on the record but are not read: nothing is drawn from them (finding D-1).

threshold

The risk the bands are relative to.

higher_is

Whether a higher prediction is the worse outcome.

subject

What one row is, in the singular.

specs

The schema's predictors.

Value

A Shiny tag, or NULL when nothing has been kept.
